categoryName: Skin care — soap, bodywash, face wash, cream, moisturiser, sunscreen, lip balm, petroleum jelly (cold hill climate)

skuLines.examples: Lifebuoy Total 10, Dettol Original & Neem, Savlon Moisture Shield, Nima
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spike Jul-Sep monsoon and any flu/infection scare
skuLines.notes: Highest-rotation bar in the lane. Multipack is the real buying unit for hostels and families; single bar must exist for a student with ₹30. Cartons soak damp in a heavy-monsoon store — keep off the floor, palletise.

skuLines.examples: Medimix 18 Herbs, Himalaya Neem & Turmeric, Chandrika, Patanjali Neem-Kanti
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon Jul-Sep (skin infection season) and year-round base
skuLines.notes: Strong fit for an institutional/Sikh campus — herbal framing, no strong perfume, vegetarian oil base. Medimix 4+1 is the classic value pack.

skuLines.examples: Mysore Sandal (150g, 3x150g), Godrej No.1 Sandal & Turmeric, Santoor PureGlo, Hamam
skuLines.seasonality: Festive/Gurpurab and gifting spikes; year-round base
skuLines.notes: Godrej No.1 pack-of-4 at ~₹96 is the price-entry family pack. Mysore Sandal doubles as a respectable gift item on a campus with visitors.

skuLines.examples: Dove Cream Beauty, Pears Pure & Gentle, Medimix Clear Glycerine, Vivel
skuLines.seasonality: Sharp Oct-Feb spike — plain soap strips skin badly in cold dry hill air
skuLines.notes: The winter soap. Shift facings from deo/lime bars to glycerin/cream bars in October; the same shelf sells the reverse in May.

skuLines.line: Deodorant / fresh soap bar for young men
skuLines.examples: Cinthol Lime & Original, Lux, Liril 2000, Nivea Fresh
skuLines.notes: Hostel-boy staple. Cinthol 100g at ~₹40 is the single most reordered impulse bar in this cluster.

skuLines.line: Soap-free / syndet bar for sensitive & eczema skin
skuLines.examples: Sebamed Cleansing Bar, Cetaphil Cleansing Bar, Aveeno Baby bar
skuLines.notes: Slow mover but there is no alternative within 30-50 km for a child with winter eczema. Stock 2-3 pieces, not a case.

skuLines.line: Institutional bulk soap carton (hostel / canteen indent)
skuLines.examples: Lifebuoy, Godrej No.1, Medimix — full cartons of 48-72 bars
skuLines.seasonality: Peaks at term start (Apr and Jul) when hostels re-stock
skuLines.notes: Warehouse counter line, not POS. Thin margin but it anchors the whole category's purchase volume and freight economics on the hill road.

skuLines.line: Body wash / shower gel — mainstream bottle
skuLines.examples: Dove Deep Moisture 800ml, Pears Pure & Gentle 750ml, Palmolive Aroma, Nivea Waterlily
skuLines.seasonality: Rich/creamy variants Oct-Feb; cooling variants Apr-Jun
skuLines.notes: Sells to salaried staff and university students, not to school students. Two SKUs (one 250ml entry, one 750ml value) beat six half-empty facings.

skuLines.examples: Nivea Men Pure Impact 500ml, Dettol Icy Cool, Fiama Men
skuLines.notes: Hair+face+body in one bottle is a genuine hostel-bathroom win; one SKU is enough.

skuLines.line: Body wash refill pouch / value litre
skuLines.examples: Fiama 900ml, Palmolive 750ml refill, Lux 750ml, Dove refill
skuLines.notes: Best rupees-per-ml on the shelf and the lowest freight weight per wash — matters when every case comes 30-50 km up a hill road.

skuLines.examples: Dettol 200ml pump, Lifebuoy 80/200ml, Santoor 200ml, Godrej Protekt
skuLines.notes: May belong to the hygiene lane — dedupe at merge. Kept here because it competes directly with the soap bar for the same handwashing occasion in hostels.

skuLines.examples: Dettol 1350ml, Savlon 1.3L, Godrej Protekt 1.5L, Lifebuoy 675ml
skuLines.notes: The pouch is what hostels, canteens and the F&V counter actually indent. Godrej Protekt powder-to-liquid 9g sachet (~₹40) is the extreme freight-light option for a hill store.

skuLines.line: Herbal neem/tulsi face wash — student entry pack
skuLines.examples: Himalaya Purifying Neem 50/100ml, Patanjali Saundarya, Boroplus face wash
skuLines.notes: The ₹15-20 50ml tube is the whole reason a 13-year-old on pocket money buys face wash at all. Never let this size go out of stock — it is the category's gateway SKU.

skuLines.line: Anti-acne / oil-control face wash for teens
skuLines.examples: Himalaya Neem, Clean & Clear Foaming, Lacto Calamine Oil Control, Garnier Men Acno Fight
skuLines.notes: Acne is the single largest skin complaint in a 5,000-person population skewed 5-25 years old. This deserves more facings than anti-ageing.

skuLines.examples: Garnier Men Turbo Bright, Himalaya Men Pimple Clear, Ponds Men, The Man Company Charcoal
skuLines.notes: Male-branded SKUs are not a gimmick here — a hostel boy will not buy a pink tube. Two SKUs cover it.

skuLines.examples: Cetaphil Gentle Skin Cleanser 118/473ml, Simple Kind To Skin, Sebamed Face Wash
skuLines.notes: Dermatologist-standard for cold dry climates. High ticket, slow turns — one 118ml facing, and a 473ml only on request/indent.

skuLines.examples: Lakme Blush & Glow, Mamaearth Vitamin C, Glow & Lovely Multivitamin, Nivea Dark Spot
skuLines.notes: Strong pull with university-age women and young staff; the claim has shifted from 'fairness' to 'glow/spots', so refresh packs rather than carrying old fairness stock.

skuLines.line: Ubtan / besan face pack & face scrub
skuLines.examples: Everyuth Walnut Scrub, Mamaearth Ubtan Face Pack, Patanjali Ubtan, Khadi Natural
skuLines.seasonality: Festive, Gurpurab, wedding season Oct-Dec and Feb-Apr
skuLines.notes: Sachet/small-tube formats move; large tubs die on the shelf. Good margin, low freight weight.

skuLines.examples: Pond's Cold Cream 100/200ml, Charmis 200ml, Dabur Gulabari, Garnier Nourishing Cold Cream 40g
skuLines.seasonality: Very sharp Oct-Feb peak; near-zero Apr-Aug
skuLines.notes: The number-one winter line for this location. Pre-book by September — a stockout in December cannot be fixed with a 30-50 km run. The 40g pack is the student/pocket size; the 200ml tub is the family size.

skuLines.examples: Nivea Soft 100/300ml, Pond's Light Moisturiser, Lakme Peach Milk, Pond's Hydra Miracle gel
skuLines.notes: Nivea Soft is the workhorse — face, hands and elbows in one jar, which is how people here actually use it.

skuLines.line: Barrier-repair / ceramide cream for very dry skin
skuLines.examples: Cetaphil Moisturising Cream 100/250g, Venusia Max, Sebamed Moisturising Cream
skuLines.notes: This is what a cold, low-humidity hill location genuinely needs and what nobody stocks. Ceramide/petrolatum-based creams are the dermatologist default for a damaged winter barrier. Two SKUs, small sizes.

skuLines.examples: Boroline 19g/40g, Boroline SX 20/40/100g, Boroplus Antiseptic 19/80/120ml
skuLines.seasonality: Huge Oct-Feb spike (chapped lips, cracked knuckles, cuts)
skuLines.notes: The most trusted single product in North Indian winter. The ₹35-45 19-20g tube is the impulse counter SKU. Ayurvedic/AYUSH-licensed product — check the label carries the AYUSH manufacturing licence number.

skuLines.examples: Himalaya Winter Defense 100ml, Nivea Creme tin 30/60/150ml, Boroplus Soft Light 200ml
skuLines.notes: The Nivea blue tin is the classic hill-station SKU — no pump to freeze, no spill in a bag. Rich creams stiffen badly below ~10°C; warn buyers rather than let them think the product has spoiled.

skuLines.examples: Pond's Age Miracle, Olay Natural White, L'Oreal Revitalift, Lotus YouthRx
skuLines.notes: Small cohort (senior staff, teachers' families). Good margin, slow turns — one or two facings maximum, and watch 24-month expiry.

skuLines.examples: Minimalist Niacinamide 10% + Zinc, The Derma Co Vitamin C, Dot & Key, Garnier Bright Complete
skuLines.notes: The 2026 growth line and the highest-margin thing in the lane. University students already know these brands from Instagram and q-commerce; carrying two SKUs stops a wallet leaking off-campus. Keep out of direct sun — vitamin C oxidises.

skuLines.examples: Patanjali Saundarya 60/150ml, Boroplus Aloe Vera 150ml, Himalaya Aloe Face Gel, Everyuth
skuLines.notes: Does five jobs (sunburn, dryness, post-shave, minor rash, hair) at a ₹49-99 price point — unusually good value density for a hill store. Water-based: risk of freeze damage in an unheated winter godown.

skuLines.examples: Vaseline Intensive Care 100/200/400ml, Nivea Body Milk, Parachute Advansed Deep Nourish, Pond's
skuLines.notes: After cold cream, the biggest rupee line in the lane. Stock the 400ml for families and the 60-100ml for students. Pump bottles seize in cold — flip-cap is the better hill pack.

skuLines.line: Intensive body cream / cocoa butter tub
skuLines.examples: Himalaya Cocoa Butter Body Cream 200ml, Vaseline Deep Restore, Boroplus Doodh Badam Kesar 400ml
skuLines.notes: Thicker than lotion; what people move to when lotion stops working in January. Tubs survive the road better than bottles.

skuLines.examples: Vaseline Original 25/60/100/200g, Vaseline Light Hydrating 42g, Boroplus Vasocare 50ml
skuLines.notes: The cheapest effective occlusive there is, and the correct answer for cracked lips, knuckles and heels at altitude. Goes rock-hard below ~10°C — store indoors and tell buyers it softens with hand warmth. The 25g tin is a pure counter-impulse SKU.

skuLines.line: Body lotion small / travel / sachet pack
skuLines.examples: Vaseline 60ml, Nivea 75ml, Ponds 50ml, brand sachets
skuLines.notes: Sachets and sub-₹60 packs are ~35% of Indian FMCG revenue for a reason. For a school student with ₹50 a week, this is the only accessible size.

skuLines.examples: Nivea Hand Cream, Vaseline Healthy Hands, Himalaya, mCaffeine Coffee Hand Cream
skuLines.notes: Real need for canteen, kitchen, laundry and housekeeping staff who have hands in cold water all winter. Nobody asks for it by name — it needs a shelf-talker.

skuLines.examples: Vaseline Derma Care Cracked Heel 25g, Patanjali Crack Heal 50g, Himalaya Footcare 50g, Krack cream
skuLines.notes: Underrated on a hill campus — cold stone floors, walking on slopes, and open footwear indoors. Patanjali 50g at ~₹54 and Vaseline 25g at ~₹75 are the two that need to be there.

skuLines.examples: The Body Shop, Plum Body Butter, mCaffeine, Nivea Body Butter
skuLines.notes: Body care premiumisation is a real 2026 trend, but a closed campus supports maybe two SKUs. Best treated as a gifting line.

skuLines.examples: Lakme Sun Expert SPF 50, Himalaya Sunprotect+ SPF 50, VLCC SPF 30, Minimalist SPF 50 PA++++
skuLines.seasonality: Mar-Jun peak, but UV is high at altitude all year and reflects off snow in winter
skuLines.notes: Underbought everywhere in hill India and genuinely justified here — UV rises with altitude and snow reflection adds more. Watch 30-36 month expiry with slow off-season rotation; negotiate near-expiry returns with the distributor before loading a case.

skuLines.examples: Cetaphil Sun Kids SPF 50+, Mamaearth Mineral Based Sunscreen, La Shield Mineral SPF 40/50
skuLines.seasonality: Mar-Jun; school sports and outdoor camps
skuLines.notes: One SKU. Real trigger is the residential school's outdoor/sports calendar — talk to wardens before buying, not after.

skuLines.examples: Lacto Calamine 60/120ml, Nycil calamine lotion, aloe after-sun gel
skuLines.notes: Doubles as oil-control lotion for teen skin, which is why it outsells pure after-sun in India.

skuLines.examples: Vaseline Rosy Lips 10g, Himalaya Lip Balm 10g, Boroline lip care, Vaseline Lip Therapy tin 17g
skuLines.notes: The cheapest impulse SKU in the entire lane and the one every single resident needs in a dry cold winter. Himalaya 10g at ~₹34 and Vaseline 10g at ~₹60 belong at the till, not on a shelf.

skuLines.examples: Nivea Caring / Cherry Shine 4.8g, Maybelline Baby Lips, Lakme Lip Love, Vaseline Aloe stick
skuLines.notes: Girls' hostel and university demand, and a common small gift. Small, light, high-margin — ideal for hill freight.

skuLines.examples: Nivea Active Care SPF, Neutrogena Norwegian Formula SPF 15, Lip Guard, Dr. Morepen lip balm
skuLines.notes: Chapped, sun-burnt lips are the classic hill complaint and an SPF balm is the actual fix. One SKU, kept at the counter through winter.

skuLines.examples: Sugar Tipsy Lips, MARS Aqua Splash Tinted, Plum Candy Melts, Lakme Lip Love
skuLines.notes: Tinted balm passes as care rather than cosmetics, which matters in a conservative institutional setting — it is the acceptable colour SKU.

skuLines.examples: Johnson's Baby 75/150g, Himalaya Baby Soap, Baby Dove, Pears Baby
skuLines.notes: May belong to a baby-care lane — dedupe at merge. Married staff families with infants have no substitute source within 30-50 km, so a stockout is a real hardship, not a lost sale.

skuLines.examples: Johnson's Top-To-Toe 200/500ml, Himalaya Baby Wash, Sebamed Baby, Mother Sparsh
skuLines.notes: One mass SKU (Johnson's/Himalaya) plus one pH-5.5 sensitive option (Sebamed/Cetaphil Baby) on indent covers the campus.

skuLines.examples: Johnson's Baby Lotion 100/200/500ml, Himalaya Baby Lotion 400ml, Mother Sparsh, Dabur Baby
skuLines.notes: Infant skin loses water fastest in cold dry air. The 100ml is the trial/pocket size; 400-500ml is the real family pack.

skuLines.examples: Johnson's Baby Cream 100/200g, Johnson's Milk+Rice 50g, Himalaya Baby Cream, Mamaearth
skuLines.notes: Thicker than baby lotion and what mothers switch to in December. The 50g Milk+Rice at ~₹96 is the volume SKU.

skuLines.examples: Himalaya Baby Diaper Rash Cream 50g, Softsens 50g, Sebamed Baby, Chicco, Cetaphil Baby
skuLines.notes: Zinc-oxide barrier cream is the one baby SKU parents will drive to town for if it is missing. Himalaya 50g at ~₹142 is the sensible single facing.

skuLines.examples: Johnson's Baby Oil 100/500ml, Dabur Lal Tail, Himalaya Baby Massage Oil, Parachute Baby
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Feb (daily winter malish is routine in North India)
skuLines.notes: Culturally non-negotiable in Punjabi/North Indian families — daily infant oil massage before a bath. Higher winter velocity than baby lotion.

skuLines.examples: Johnson's Baby Powder 100/200/400g, Himalaya Baby Powder, Pigeon
skuLines.notes: Cakes and clumps in a damp monsoon godown — buy short, store dry, avoid overloading before the rains.

skuLines.examples: Himalaya Baby Wipes, Mother Sparsh Water Wipes, Pampers, Johnson's
skuLines.notes: Dry out if the pack seal is broken or stored warm; rotate on FIFO. Multi-pack buying is the norm for families who cannot re-buy easily.

skuLines.examples: Ponds Dreamflower, Cinthol, Shower to Shower Ayurvedic, Navratna Cool Talc 400g
skuLines.notes: Adjacent to the lane but sits on the same shelf and buys the same occasion. Shower to Shower 150g around ₹62-67 is the value entry.

skuLines.examples: Nycil Germ Expert 150/400g, Dermi Cool 150g+60g, Candid Prickly Heat 120g, Boroplus Icy Cool
skuLines.seasonality: Apr-Jul, and again in humid Aug-Sep
skuLines.notes: Genuine hostel problem in a humid pre-monsoon month with shared bathrooms. Nycil and Dermi Cool are the two names people ask for; the 150g+60g free pack is the standard buy.

skuLines.examples: Dabur Gulabari Rose Water 120/250ml, plain glycerin 100/200ml, Patanjali gulab jal
skuLines.notes: The traditional low-cost winter moisturiser older residents actually reach for — glycerin mixed with rose water. Cheap, high margin, light to freight, and nothing else substitutes for it in this cohort.

skuLines.examples: Dettol Antiseptic Liquid 125/250/550ml, Savlon Antiseptic
skuLines.notes: Hygiene-lane overlap — dedupe at merge. Kept here because on a residential campus it is bought for bathing water and minor wounds, not for floors.

skuLines.examples: Candid / Clotrimazole cream, Itch Guard, Ring Guard, Abzorb dusting powder
skuLines.notes: Fungal infection in shared hostel bathrooms during a heavy monsoon is a predictable annual event. LICENCE CONSTRAINT: allopathic antifungals are drugs under the Drugs & Cosmetics Act and need a retail drug licence (Form 20/21) with a registered pharmacist — a general store cannot legally stock them. Ayurvedic/AYUSH-licensed alternatives can be stocked; otherwise route to the campus dispensary.

skuLines.examples: Mysore Sandal gift box, Nivea winter gift pack, Vaseline+lip balm combo, Himalaya gift hamper
skuLines.seasonality: Gurpurab, Diwali, staff recognition, visiting-parent season
skuLines.notes: A campus with 5,000 residents, visitors and staff functions has real gifting demand and no gift shop. Assemble in-store from existing stock rather than buying vendor hampers — better margin and no dead inventory.

trends2026: Sun care is the fastest-growing skincare sub-segment in India — SPF 50 PA++++ hybrid gels have dropped into the ₹250-500 mass band (Himalaya Sunprotect+ ~₹244, Lakme 9to5 ~₹336, Minimalist ~₹379), and mineral/kids SPF has entered mainstream retail. Statista's outlook puts sun protection near $2.8bn by 2031, growing faster than the face segment it sits inside.

'Skin barrier repair' has replaced fairness as the claim that sells. Ceramides, panthenol, squalane and petrolatum-led occlusives are now on mass packs; dermatologist guidance for cold/dry climates is explicitly ceramide-cream-first, which maps directly onto a hill location.

Ingredient-led actives went mass: niacinamide 10%, vitamin C, alpha-arbutin and salicylic acid at ₹235-670 from D2C brands (Minimalist, The Derma Co, Dot & Key, Foxtale). University-age buyers ask for the molecule, not the brand.
Body care is premiumising into 'body as skincare' — serum-in-lotion, body SPF (Vaseline Sun Protect SPF 30, mCaffeine SPF 30 body lotion), body butters, and 750-900ml value body-wash bottles.

'Modern Ayurveda' with ingredient transparency has displaced generic 'herbal' — Mamaearth Ubtan/Vitamin C cold creams, Nat Habit, Kapiva, alongside the old guard (Medimix, Boroline, Patanjali) which still holds the winter shelf.

Quick commerce (Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart) is now a top BPC channel and sets the price a student checks on their phone. India's online BPC market is around ₹56,000 Cr growing ~35% YoY — a closed township store is benchmarked against 10-minute pricing it cannot be compared to on service.
Men's skincare has moved past face wash into men's moisturiser, men's SPF and 3-in-1 body wash — relevant to a large male university and staff cohort.

Sachet and sub-₹60 packs remain the actual access format: small packs are roughly 35% of Indian FMCG revenue, and the ₹15-20 50ml face wash / ₹35 19g Boroline / ₹30-60 lip balm tier is what a school student on pocket money can buy.
adjacentServices: Pre-packed 'Winter Kit' sold at hostel intake and to visiting parents — glycerin soap + body lotion + cold cream + lip balm + petroleum jelly, one price, one decision. Turns the Oct-Feb spike into a pre-booked order instead of a December stockout.

Standing monthly warden/hostel/canteen indent for soap cartons, handwash refill pouches and jelly through the warehouse counter — predictable volume that fixes the freight economics for the whole category.
'New baby on campus' starter kit for married staff families — baby soap, wash, lotion, cream, rash cream, massage oil — offered when a family arrives or a birth is registered.

Refill / value-pack counter: handwash pouches, 750-900ml body wash, large lotion packs priced per-ml against the small pack, so families can see the saving. Lower freight weight per wash up the hill road.

Problem-based shelf signage in Punjabi and Hindi (dry/cracked skin, chapped lips, pimples, baby rash, prickly heat) — there is no beauty advisor on campus, and hand cream, heel cream and SPF lip balm only sell when someone names the problem.

Seasonal pre-book programme with distributors: commit Oct-Feb winter stock in September, and negotiate near-expiry return or exchange on sunscreen before loading a case, since off-season rotation is slow at 30-50 km from the nearest market.

Licensed OTC corner or a referral protocol to the campus dispensary for antifungal and medicated creams — a retail drug licence with a registered pharmacist is required for allopathic antifungals; AYUSH-licensed alternatives can sit on the general shelf.
In-store gift-pack assembly from existing stock for Gurpurab, Diwali, staff recognition and visitor gifting — margin without the dead inventory of vendor hampers.

Vegetarian-ingredient labelling shelf tag (sodium cocoate / palm kernelate vs sodium tallowate) — meaningful in a Sikh institution where many residents are vegetarian, and most Indian soap packs do not state the fat source.
